pc.structure_note: A Professional Corporation (PC) is a true corporation -- genuinely distinct from a Professional Association (PA), which is not (see pa.json's structure_note). A PC uses real shareholders and stock, with statutory share-transfer restrictions (Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 303.003) not present in a plain for-profit corporation. Unlike a PA, a PC is not restricted to a narrow enumerated list of professions -- it is the general-purpose professional-corporation vehicle used across most licensed professions (attorneys, CPAs, engineers, architects, and others not on the PA-specific medical/health list). Most categories below mirror corporation.json directly since the base corporate governance/financial/operational mechanics are the same entity; the professional_licensing_compliance category is the genuinely new layer, driven by Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Chapter 301's ownership/licensing restrictions, which apply to a PC the same way they apply to a PLLC or PA.

identity: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status
Shareholder Agreement (with Professional Ownership Transfer Restrictions)
statutory: Texas Business Organizations Code Chapter 303 Compliance
Texas Business Organizations Code Chapter 301 Compliance (professional-entity ownership/licensing restrictions)
Texas Franchise Tax Public Information Report (PIR) Filing
Foreign Qualification Filings (if operating in other states)
records_transparency: Stock Transfer Documents (subject to Section 303.003 restrictions)
professional_licensing_compliance: Professional Organization Ownership Documentation (if an owner is itself a qualifying professional organization rather than an individual)
Entity Name Compliance Certification (professional designator and governing-profession ethics-rule check)
State Licensing Board Registration (the specific board depends on the profession -- e.g. TSBPA for a CPA-owned PC, State Bar of Texas for an attorney-owned PC, TBPELS for an engineer-owned PC)

Certificate of Formation (Professional C: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 1, Chapter 3, Subchapter A (general formation), Title 2, Chapters 20 and 21 (for-profit corporation provisions), and Title 7, Chapter 303 (PC-specific provisions) -- filed via Secretary of State Form 203, distinct from the PA Form 204 and PLLC Form 206. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 203 instructions.
Stock Certificates: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 303.002 (Authority and Liability of Shareholder) and Section 303.003 (Notice of Restriction on Transfer of Shares) -- PC shares carry statutory transfer restrictions tied to professional-licensing eligibility that plain for-profit corporation shares do not.
Shareholder Agreement (with Professional: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 303.003 (transfer restriction notice requirement) and Section 303.004 (redemption of shares, price and terms) -- these govern what happens when a shareholder loses professional eligibility (e.g. license lapse, death, disqualification) and must divest.
Texas Business Organizations Code Chapte: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 7, Chapter 303, applying Title 2 Chapters 20/21 (for-profit corporation provisions) alongside PC-specific rules. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 203 instructions.

Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 301.001(a) confirms Title 7 (including Chapter 301's ownership/licensing restrictions) applies to professional corporations, professional associations, and PLLCs alike -- explicitly excluding partnerships and LLPs (Section 301.001(c)). Section 301.007's individual-licensing requirement for owners/officers, already used in pllc.json, applies here the same way.
Workers' Compensation Policy: Tex. Labor Code Section 406.002 -- Texas is the only state in the country where workers' compensation coverage is elective, not mandatory, for most private employers. An employer who opts out ('non-subscriber') must notify the Texas Division of Workers' Compensation (Section 406.004) and notify employees (Section 406.005), and forfeits certain common-law defenses in the event of a workplace injury lawsuit. EXCEPTION: coverage is mandatory for government building/construction contracts under Section 406.096. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 across multiple independent sources; added retroactively as a batch correction across all deployed entity-type files that list this document type.
